extracted.intended_audience: mathematics teachers and students (authors of proofs and homework write-ups)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing and evaluating mathematical exposition and proofs, aimed at teachers preparing materials and students preparing homework, focusing on clarity, notation, style, and proofreading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Include enough explanation so that the intended reader can follow what you are saying; style differs for fellow teachers/journals versus students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include every detail all the time — it is fine to expect the reader to be actively involved — but do not skip details that would require the reader to spend hours filling them in. This applies in particular to course assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give yourself time to do the writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow enough time to write and revise rather than rushing a few minutes before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having time lets you read your work for sense, correct spelling, choose right words, fix grammar, and improve organization. Writing well is much harder when rushed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the reader informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the reader what you plan to do, then do it; comment on structure and steps in proofs and exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State assumptions and identify the proof technique (e.g., 'We will give a direct proof'). If using previous propositions, point them out and name them if possible. If a used result has no name, indicate its content. Define new or uncommon symbols/terms. Avoid roadblocks—use phrases like 'Now (or Next) we show that...' to signal intent. Indicate explicitly when a proof is finished (symbol, 'QED', or words). Avoid saying 'clearly' or 'obvious' unless it truly is obvious to the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make mathematical symbols stand out from prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables, equations, names of sets, etc., should be visually distinct from running text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use italics for variables and similar items. Display mathematical expressions on separate centered lines (same for computations) rather than inline chaining long equations; break multi-step computations across separate lines for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not begin a sentence with a mathematical symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid starting sentences with symbols; restructure so a word begins the sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of 'n ∈ Z, so we have ...' write 'If n ∈ Z, then we have ...' or similar phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate symbols not in a list by words when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Use words to separate standalone symbols for clarity rather than relying solely on punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., write 'Except for a, the number b is the only root of the equation ...' rather than 'Except for a, b is the only root ...'. Commas are fine to separate items in lists like 'Let a, b, c ∈ Z.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the pronoun 'we' instead of 'I'
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'we' to include reader and writer jointly in proofs and exposition; avoid sounding conceited with 'I'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'We will now show that G is a group' or 'Let's show that G is a group.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid informal and colloquial language
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not write as if speaking colloquially; prefer formal mathematical phrasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filler words like 'like', 'you know', slang ('Get my drift, man? (Dude?)'). Use 'substitute 7 for x' instead of 'plug 7 in for x'. Avoid foul or suggestive language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be familiar with common mathematical words and phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard mathematical terms appropriately and with variety when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words like 'each' and 'every' are interchangeable in many contexts; synonyms such as 'therefore', 'thus', 'hence', 'consequently' mean the same — avoid monotonous repetition. Avoid awkward constructions like 'Since ..., then ...' and prefer alternatives such as 'If ..., then ...' or 'Since ..., it follows that ...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use words for numbers in running prose
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a number as part of an English sentence, prefer the word form rather than the numeral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write 'The difference between x and y is zero.' rather than '... is 0.' Avoid mixing words and symbols improperly: prefer 'Every integer greater than or equal to two ...' or 'If n ≥ 2 is an integer, then ...'. Avoid unnecessary symbols in general statements (e.g., omit a symbol in a general theorem statement unless needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain and be consistent in the use of symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the meaning of every symbol used (fixed symbols like Z or ∪ need definition only at first use); be consistent and choose conventional symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not change notation mid-proof. When defining related quantities, use alphabetical order or subscripts. Follow common conventions (real variables: u,v,x,y; integers: k,n,m,p,q; functions: f,g,h; p,q for polynomials) and pay attention to conventions from class or reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid passive voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer active constructions to make writing clearer and more direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide gives this as general advice with no long elaboration; rephrase passive sentences into active voice where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use good grammar, spelling, and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure correct grammar and spelling and organize proofs so they flow logically without jumping around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you reach a stage in a proof that requires something mentioned earlier, rewrite the proof in the proper order rather than inserting 'I forgot to mention that ...'. Use paragraphs and logical sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly (re)state the problem to be solved
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin solutions/homework write-ups by clearly restating the problem or what is to be proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first checklist question in the homework-evaluation checklist; restating helps the reader understand the target of the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the solution self-contained
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the solution contains all information needed to follow the argument without requiring undue external lookup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include necessary definitions or references so the intended reader can verify steps; balance self-containment with not repeating entire textbooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include an appropriate amount of detail for the intended reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the level of justification and intermediate steps appropriate to the reader's background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid both excessive trivial detail and gaps that force the reader to supply long missing arguments; tailor detail to audience (see 'Know your audience').

rubrics_metrics.name: Write solutions in complete sentences with attention to grammar and spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical solutions should be written in complete sentences and proofread for grammar and spelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor sentence structure or spelling reduces clarity; use full sentences where needed rather than disjointed fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use paragraphs where necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize solutions and proofs into paragraphs to group related ideas and steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph breaks help readability, especially in longer arguments or when changing proof stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include remarks in proofs to help the reader understand reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Add brief explanatory comments or remarks to highlight strategy, intent, or nontrivial steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks can indicate why a step is taken, which technique is being used, or provide intuition; they should aid, not distract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly label diagrams, tables, and graphs
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures used should be clearly labeled for reference and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions, axis labels, and notation in figures must be explicit so the figure is immediately informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly define all variables and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure every variable and symbol used is defined for the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a symbol is used only later or is nonstandard, define it where introduced. Fixed symbols need definition at first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate unnecessary variables and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid introducing symbols that are not needed for the argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simpler notation improves clarity; remove redundant variables or notation where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly reference definitions, theorems, and formulas used
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying known results, cite or reference them explicitly so the reader can verify the step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use names for standard results when available ('By the Pythagorean Theorem, ...'). If unnamed, indicate the relevant content or where to find it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give acknowledgment where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge sources, ideas, or collaborators when they contribute to the solution or exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite sources for nontrivial lemmas, borrowed examples, or assistance received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer the question that was asked
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure the submission addresses the stated problem and does not stray into unrelated results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restate the problem and verify the final statement matches the question asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check that the mathematics is correct
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify computations, logical steps, and correctness of claims before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread for mathematical correctness as well as language; confirm conclusions follow from assumptions and intermediate steps.
